statement: AI infrastructure investment is projected at $1.3 trillion in 2027, a 60% year-over-year increase, with memory's share of that spend rising from 14% in 2025 to 57%.
why: A 60% step-up in total AI infrastructure spend sets the size of the pool that GPU, memory and system vendors compete for, and the shift of that pool toward memory changes what a given dollar buys.

impact.mechanism: A larger overall AI capex pool lifts accelerator demand, but memory taking 57% of the spend versus 14% two years earlier crowds out the share available for GPUs and other system content.

evidence.excerpt: Key figures cited: AI infrastructure investment is projected at $1.3 trillion next year, a 60% increase year-over-year. Memory's share of AI infrastructure spending is described as expanding from 14% in 2025, to 40% in the current year (2026), to 57% next year (2027).

confidence.basis: Sell-side projection (KB Securities) carried by a single secondary outlet; forward forecast rather than reported spend.

dispersion: Memory share path is steep and uncertain: 14% (2025) to 40% (2026) to 57% (2027).
